examples.en: My balance is at zero.

notes: Becomes 'un' before a masc. noun (un taco) and 'una' before a fem. noun (una hora).

examples.en: Give me one, please.
It's two blocks straight ahead.
I have three siblings.

examples.tl: El Uber llega en cuatro minutos.
examples.en: The Uber arrives in four minutes.
It costs five pesos.
See you at six.
That's seven fifty.

examples.tl: La reunión es a las ocho.
examples.en: The meeting is at eight.
I live on the ninth floor.
Ten more minutes, please.

notes: Spelled 'once', not 'onze'. In Chile 'la once' = afternoon tea/snack.

examples.tl: El vuelo sale a las once.
examples.en: The flight leaves at eleven.

examples.tl: Son las doce, vamos a comer.
examples.en: It's twelve, let's go eat.
My nephew is thirteen.
Today is February 14th.

notes: 'Quince días' = two weeks. 'Los quince años' = the big 15th-birthday party (quinceañera). 'Quincena' = biweekly paycheck.

examples.en: I'll be back in two weeks.

notes: One word, accent on the é. 16–19 all start with 'dieci-'.

examples.en: The appointment is on the 16th.

examples.tl: Hay diecisiete personas en la lista.
examples.en: There are seventeen people on the list.

examples.tl: Ya tiene dieciocho, ya puede votar.
examples.en: He's eighteen now, he can vote.
It's nineteen dollars.

notes: 21–29 are one word: veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés, veinticuatro... (accents on veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis).

examples.tl: Te mando veinte pesos por la app.
examples.en: I'll send you twenty pesos through the app.

notes: From 31 up, numbers are separate words with 'y': treinta y uno, cuarenta y dos.

examples.en: I'm thirty-two years old.
It's forty minutes by subway.
Can you change a fifty for me?
An hour has sixty minutes.

notes: Don't mix up setenta (70) and sesenta (60).

examples.en: My dad is seventy.
The taxi charges eighty pesos.
My visa lasts ninety days.

notes: 'Cien' alone or right before a noun (cien pesos). 'Ciento' in 101–199 (ciento diez) and in 'por ciento' (percent).

examples.en: It's a hundred pesos an hour.

notes: No 'y' after ciento: ciento uno, ciento veinte, ciento cincuenta. 'Ciento un' before a masc. noun.

examples.tl: Estoy en el cuarto ciento uno.
examples.en: I'm in room 101.

notes: Agrees in gender: doscientas personas. 300 trescientos, 400 cuatrocientos, 600 seiscientos, 800 ochocientos.

examples.tl: El vuelo me salió en doscientos dólares.
examples.en: The flight came out to two hundred dollars.

notes: Irregular (not 'cincocientos'). Also irregular: setecientos (700) and novecientos (900).

examples.en: Do you have change for a five hundred?

notes: No 'un': 'mil pesos', never 'un mil'. 2,000 = dos mil. 'Miles de' = thousands of.

examples.tl: La renta es de doce mil pesos.
examples.en: The rent is twelve thousand pesos.

notes: It's a noun: 'un millón DE pesos'. Plural: dos millones. A US billion = 'mil millones' (not 'un billón').

examples.tl: Ese depa cuesta más de un millón.
examples.en: That apartment costs more than a million.

notes: Shortens to 'primer' before a masc. noun: el primer día. Fem: primera. Dates: 'el primero de mayo'.

examples.tl: Es mi primer viaje a Colombia.
examples.en: It's my first trip to Colombia.

notes: Fem: segunda. Also the noun 'un segundo' = a second (of time).

examples.en: I live on the second floor.

notes: Shortens to 'tercer' before a masc. noun: el tercer piso. Fem: tercera.

examples.tl: Es la tercera vez que te llamo.
examples.en: It's the third time I've called you.

notes: Also a noun: 'un cuarto' = a quarter (un cuarto de kilo) or a room/bedroom (Mex).

examples.en: Get off at the fourth stop.
We're on the fifth floor.

examples.tl: Mi hija va en sexto de primaria.
examples.en: My daughter is in sixth grade.

examples.tl: Julio es el séptimo mes del año.
examples.en: July is the seventh month of the year.
I live on the eighth floor.
He finished in ninth place.

notes: Past ten, people just use the plain number: 'el piso once', 'el aniversario veinte'.

examples.en: This is my tenth try.

notes: Agrees with the noun: medio kilo, media hora, medio litro. 'Y media' = half past. The noun is 'la mitad'.

examples.en: Give me half a kilo of tortillas.

notes: 'Un par de' = a couple of (loosely two or three). 'Un par de zapatos' = a pair of shoes.

examples.en: Wait for me a couple of minutes.

notes: 'Media docena' = half a dozen. Eggs and bread are often sold by the dozen or by the piece.

examples.tl: Una docena de huevos, por favor.
examples.en: A dozen eggs, please.

notes: Agrees: ¿cuántos tacos? ¿cuántas personas? Singular '¿cuánto?' = how much.

examples.en: How old are you?
How many people are you?

notes: Fem: todas. Singular 'todo' = everything. 'Todos los días' = every day. 'Todo el mundo' = everybody.

examples.en: Everyone's here now.

notes: '¿Tienes hora?' = Do you have the time? 'Es hora de...' = it's time to... 'Hora pico' = rush hour.

examples.en: Do you have the time?
It took me an hour to get there.

notes: '¿Qué horas son?' is very common in Mexico and Colombia. Answer with 'Es la una' or 'Son las [number]'.

examples.tl: Perdón, ¿qué hora es? —Son las tres y diez.
examples.en: Sorry, what time is it? —It's 3:10.

notes: Singular 'es la' only for 1:00–1:59. Every other hour uses 'son las'.

examples.tl: Es la una y veinte, vamos a comer.
examples.en: It's 1:20, let's go eat.

notes: Pattern: son las [hour] y [minutes]. 'Y media' = :30, 'y cuarto' = :15, 'y diez' = :10.

examples.tl: Son las dos y media y todavía no llega el Uber.
examples.en: It's two thirty and the Uber still isn't here.

notes: 'Las cinco y cuarto' = 5:15. Many people just say 'y quince'.

examples.tl: Nos vemos a las seis y cuarto.
examples.en: See you at a quarter past six.

notes: 'Las siete menos cuarto' = 6:45. In Mexico/Colombia you'll also hear 'un cuarto para las siete' or 'faltan quince para las siete'.

examples.en: It's a quarter to eight.

examples.tl: Es un cuarto para las ocho.
examples.en: It's a quarter to eight.

notes: After a clock time: las 7 de la mañana. 'De la tarde' = p.m. until ~7–8; 'de la noche' = evening/night. 24h time is for tickets and schedules; speech uses 12h.

examples.tl: El vuelo sale a las seis de la mañana.
examples.en: The flight leaves at six a.m.

examples.tl: La cena es a las ocho de la noche.
examples.en: Dinner is at eight p.m.

notes: 'Al mediodía' = at noon. Since lunch is often 2–3 pm, 'mediodía' can loosely mean early afternoon.

examples.en: We eat at noon.

notes: 'A medianoche' = at midnight. The hours after it are 'la madrugada'.

examples.en: We arrived at midnight.

notes: Roughly 1–6 a.m. 'Las tres de la madrugada' = 3 a.m. 'Madrugar' = to get up very early.

examples.tl: El vuelo sale a las cuatro de la madrugada.
examples.en: The flight leaves at four in the morning.

notes: 'A las' + hour = at. Only 1:00 takes 'a la una'. 'A las ocho en punto' = at eight sharp.

examples.tl: La cita es a las ocho.
examples.en: The appointment is at eight.

notes: Answer with 'a las...': ¿A qué hora abren? —A las nueve.

examples.en: What time do they open?

notes: Colloquial approximation (Mex, Arg, Col): 'tipo ocho' / 'tipo las ocho'. Neutral options: 'como a las ocho', 'a eso de las ocho'.

examples.en: I'll get there around eight, okay?

notes: 'Un minutito' = just a sec. 'Al minuto' = instantly.

examples.en: Give me five minutes.

notes: 'Un segundo' = one sec. Same word as the ordinal 'second'.

examples.en: One second, I'm coming.

notes: 'Media' agrees with fem. 'hora'. 'Hora y media' = an hour and a half.

examples.en: The Uber takes half an hour.

notes: 'Por ahora' = for now. 'Hasta ahora' = so far. 'Ahora sí' = now we're talking / this time yes.

examples.tl: Ahora no puedo, te marco luego.
examples.en: I can't right now, I'll call you later.

notes: Famously ambiguous (Mex/Central Am): 'right now', 'in a little while' or a polite 'maybe never'. 'Ahorita voy' may mean 20 min. Caribbean: = later.

examples.en: I'll send it to you in a sec.
—Are you coming? —I'm on my way (soon-ish).

notes: Very flexible: already / now / enough. '¡Ya!' = Stop! / Done! 'Ya no' = not anymore. 'Ya voy' = I'm coming.

examples.en: Did you eat already?
I don't live there anymore.

notes: 'Todavía no' = not yet. 'Aún' means the same but is more written/formal.

examples.en: The package hasn't arrived yet.

notes: 'Hasta luego' = see you later. 'Luego luego' (Mex) = right away. 'Desde luego' = of course.

examples.tl: Te hablo luego, estoy en el banco.
examples.en: I'll call you later, I'm at the bank.

notes: 'Después de' + noun/infinitive: después de comer. Near-synonym of 'luego'.

examples.tl: Después del trabajo vamos por unos tacos.
examples.en: After work we're going for tacos.

notes: 'Antes de' + noun/infinitive: antes de salir. 'Cuanto antes' = as soon as possible.

examples.en: Call me before you come over.

notes: 'Hoy en día' = nowadays. 'Hoy no' = not today.

examples.en: They're not open today, it's a holiday.

notes: Also the noun 'la mañana' = morning. 'Mañana en la mañana' = tomorrow morning. 'Hasta mañana' = see you tomorrow.

examples.en: Tomorrow I have an appointment at immigration.
Yesterday I went to the market.

notes: One word. 'Anteanoche' = the night before last.

examples.en: It rained a ton last night.

notes: 'Antier' is the everyday form in Mexico and much of LatAm; 'anteayer' is standard everywhere and the only form in Spain.

examples.en: I got back from Bogotá the day before yesterday.
The flight is the day after tomorrow.

notes: Both 'at that time' and 'so/therefore'. Common sentence opener: 'Entonces, ¿qué hacemos?'

examples.tl: Entonces nos vemos a las siete.
examples.en: So we'll see each other at seven, then.

notes: 'Como siempre' = as usual. 'Para siempre' = forever. 'Casi siempre' = almost always.

examples.en: I always order the same thing.

notes: 'Seguido' is the spoken LatAm word (Mex, Col). 'A menudo' is more formal/written. 'Muy seguido' = very often.

examples.en: Do you come here often?

notes: 'De vez en cuando' = once in a while. 'A veces sí, a veces no.'

examples.en: Sometimes I work from home.

notes: 'Casi nunca' (almost never) is more common in speech.

examples.en: I rarely go out on weekdays.

notes: Double negative is normal: 'No voy nunca'. When 'nunca' comes before the verb, drop 'no': 'Nunca voy'.

examples.en: I've never been to Oaxaca.

notes: Stronger than 'nunca'. 'Nunca jamás' = never ever.

examples.en: I'm never going back to that restaurant.

notes: 'Enseguida' and 'luego luego' (Mex) also mean right away.

examples.tl: Si ves algo raro, avísame de inmediato.
examples.en: If you see anything weird, let me know immediately.

notes: 'Un momentito' is softer. On the phone with usted: 'Espere un momento, por favor.'

examples.tl: Un momento, por favor, ya le atiendo.
examples.en: One moment please, I'll be right with you.

notes: 'Un rato' = a while; '-ito' makes it shorter and friendlier. 'Al rato' (Mex) = later today. 'Hace rato' = a while ago.

examples.tl: Espérame un ratito, ya casi termino.
examples.en: Wait for me a little while, I'm almost done.

notes: 'Más temprano' = earlier. 'Tempranito' = nice and early.

examples.en: Tomorrow I'm getting up early.

notes: Adverb 'tarde' = late; the noun 'la tarde' = afternoon. 'Se me hizo tarde' = I'm running late. 'Más tarde' = later.

examples.en: Sorry, I got here late.

notes: 'Llegar a tiempo' = to arrive on time. 'Puntual' = punctual. 'Justo a tiempo' = just in time.

examples.tl: El bus llegó justo a tiempo.
examples.en: The bus arrived just in time.

notes: 'Entre semana' = on weekdays. 'Fin de semana' = weekend. 'La semana que viene' = next week.

examples.en: I'm very busy this week.

notes: Plural: meses. 'Al mes' = per month. 'Cada mes' = every month.

examples.tl: Pago la renta el primero de cada mes.
examples.en: I pay rent on the first of every month.

notes: 'Tener X años' = to be X years old. 'Año Nuevo' = New Year. Never drop the ñ: 'ano' means anus.

examples.en: I've been living here a year.

notes: Masculine despite the -a: el día, buenos días. 'Al día' = per day / up to date. 'Todo el día' = all day.

examples.en: What day is it today?

notes: 'Buenas noches' = good evening / good night. 'En la noche' (LatAm) or 'por la noche' = at night.

examples.tl: En la noche hay más tráfico.
examples.en: At night there's more traffic.

notes: 'En la mañana' (LatAm) / 'por la mañana' = in the morning. Same word as the adverb 'mañana' = tomorrow.

examples.en: In the morning I work out.

notes: Runs from about noon to sunset (~7–8 pm). 'Buenas tardes' = good afternoon. 'En la tarde' = in the afternoon.

examples.en: See you this afternoon.

notes: Colloquially 'el fin' or 'el finde'. 'Este fin' = this weekend. 'Los fines de semana' = on weekends.

examples.tl: ¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?
examples.en: What are you doing this weekend?

notes: 'La semana que viene' and (Mex) 'la semana que entra' are just as common. Same for 'el próximo mes', 'el año que viene'.

examples.tl: La próxima semana tengo cita en el consulado.
examples.en: Next week I have an appointment at the consulate.

notes: 'Pasado' after the noun = last: la semana pasada, el año pasado, el lunes pasado.

examples.tl: El mes pasado la luz salió carísima.
examples.en: Last month the electric bill was super expensive.

notes: The normal spoken form. 'Cada día' = each day. 'Diario' (Mex) = daily. Same pattern: todas las semanas, todos los meses.

examples.tl: Camino al trabajo todos los días.
examples.en: I walk to work every day.

notes: In Mexico 'diario' alone = every day: 'voy diario'. Also the noun 'el diario' = newspaper (Arg/Col) or diary.

examples.tl: Como en ese puesto casi diario.
examples.en: I eat at that stand almost every day.

notes: 'Hasta luego / hasta mañana'. Mexican quirk: 'abren hasta las diez' = they don't open until ten.

examples.en: I work until six.

notes: 'Desde las ocho' = since/from eight. 'Desde que' + clause = ever since. 'Desde hace' + duration = for.

examples.en: I've lived here since January.

notes: 'Hace' + time = ago: hace un rato, hace una hora, hace mucho. Goes with the preterite.

examples.tl: Hace dos años me mudé a México.
examples.en: Two years ago I moved to Mexico.

notes: 'Desde hace tres meses' = for three months (and counting), with the present tense. Alternative: 'llevo tres meses + gerund'.

examples.tl: Estudio español desde hace tres meses.
examples.en: I've been studying Spanish for three months.

notes: '¡Hace mucho (tiempo)!' = It's been a while! 'Tardar mucho' = to take a long time.

examples.tl: ¡Hace mucho tiempo que no te veía!
examples.en: I hadn't seen you in a long time!

notes: 'Hasta pronto' = see you soon. 'Tan pronto como' = as soon as. 'De pronto' = suddenly (in Colombia also 'maybe').

examples.en: See you soon.

notes: Works as adjective and adverb in speech: 'maneja rápido'. '¡Rápido!' = Hurry up!

examples.tl: Llegamos rápido porque no había tráfico.
examples.en: We got there fast because there was no traffic.

notes: 'Más despacio, por favor' = slower, please (a learner's best friend). The adjective is 'lento'.

examples.en: Could you speak more slowly, please?

notes: Days are lowercase and masculine. 'El lunes' = on Monday; 'los lunes' = on Mondays. LatAm calendars start the week on Monday.

examples.tl: El lunes tengo cita con el dentista.
examples.en: On Monday I have a dentist appointment.

notes: 'Martes trece' is the unlucky date (like Friday the 13th).

examples.en: Today is Tuesday.

notes: Accent on the é. Days ending in -s have the same form singular and plural: el/los miércoles.

examples.tl: Los miércoles hay tianguis en mi colonia.
examples.en: On Wednesdays there's a street market in my neighborhood.
My flight leaves on Thursday.

notes: 'Viernes de quincena' (Mex) = payday Friday, when everyone goes out.

examples.en: It's finally Friday!

notes: Plural: sábados. Accent on the first á.

examples.tl: El sábado hay fiesta en casa de mi cuñado.
examples.en: Saturday there's a party at my brother-in-law's.

notes: Plural: domingos. In Mexico 'el domingo' also = a kid's weekly allowance.

examples.tl: Los domingos comemos en casa de mi suegra.
examples.en: On Sundays we eat at my mother-in-law's.

notes: Months are lowercase. 'En enero' = in January. Dates: 'el 5 de enero'.

examples.tl: En enero hace frío en la Ciudad de México.
examples.en: In January it's cold in Mexico City.

examples.tl: El 14 de febrero es el Día del Amor y la Amistad.
examples.en: February 14th is Valentine's Day (Day of Love and Friendship).
Spring starts in March.
My birthday is in April.

notes: 'El 10 de mayo' = Mother's Day in Mexico (fixed date). 'Cinco de Mayo' is a minor holiday there.

examples.tl: El 10 de mayo es el Día de las Madres en México.
examples.en: May 10th is Mother's Day in Mexico.
The rains start in June.

notes: Don't confuse junio (June) and julio (July).

examples.tl: En julio hay vacaciones en las escuelas.
examples.en: In July schools are on vacation.

examples.tl: Agosto es muy caluroso en Monterrey.
examples.en: August is very hot in Monterrey.

notes: Also spelled 'setiembre' in Peru, Costa Rica and parts of South America. Mexican Independence Day: 16 de septiembre.

examples.tl: El 15 de septiembre se celebra la Independencia.
examples.en: Independence is celebrated on September 15th (the night before).

examples.tl: En octubre empieza a hacer frío.
examples.en: In October it starts to get cold.

examples.tl: El 2 de noviembre es el Día de Muertos.
examples.en: November 2nd is the Day of the Dead.

notes: 'Las posadas' (Dec 16–24) and 'el aguinaldo' (year-end bonus) are big in Mexico.

examples.tl: En diciembre viajo a ver a mi familia.
examples.en: In December I travel to see my family.

notes: Not a romantic date (that's 'cita'). 'Fecha de vencimiento' = expiration date. Written order is day/month/year: 5/10 = 5 de octubre.

examples.en: What's the expiration date?

notes: Answer: 'Hoy es once de octubre.' The 1st uses 'primero': 'el primero de mayo'. Other days use plain numbers.

examples.tl: —¿Qué fecha es hoy? —Es once de octubre.
examples.en: —What's the date today? —It's October 11th.

notes: Same form singular and plural: el cumpleaños. '¡Feliz cumpleaños!' Colloquial: 'el cumple'. 'Cumplir años' = to have a birthday.

examples.en: When is your birthday?

notes: In LatAm 'clima' = today's weather, not just climate: '¿Cómo está el clima?'. Spain says 'el tiempo'. Masculine despite -a.

examples.en: How's the weather in Monterrey?

notes: Time as duration, and also weather. 'No tengo tiempo' = I don't have time. For clock time use 'hora'. 'Hace buen tiempo' = nice weather.

examples.en: I don't have time, I'm running late.
In spring the jacarandas bloom.

notes: In much of Mexico/Central America 'verano' overlaps with the rainy season; the hottest months are often April–May.

examples.tl: En verano vamos a la playa.
examples.en: In summer we go to the beach.
In the fall the leaves drop.

notes: South of the equator (Argentina, Chile) winter is June–August.

examples.tl: El invierno en Bogotá no es tan frío.
examples.en: Winter in Bogotá isn't that cold.

notes: Roughly June–October in Mexico and Central America. 'Temporada' = season (also sports/TV). Dry season = 'temporada de secas'.

examples.tl: En temporada de lluvias llueve casi todas las tardes.
examples.en: In the rainy season it rains almost every afternoon.

notes: Double l. 'Bajo la lluvia' = in the rain. 'Paraguas' = umbrella.

examples.tl: Con la lluvia, el tráfico está peor.
examples.en: With the rain, the traffic is worse.

notes: From 'llover' (o>ue), used only in the 3rd person. 'Está lloviendo' = it's raining right now. 'Llovió' = it rained.

examples.tl: Si llueve, nos quedamos en casa.
examples.en: If it rains, we're staying home.

notes: 'Un día soleado'. For right now people more often say 'hace sol' or 'está soleado'.

examples.en: Tomorrow it's going to be sunny.

notes: Weather uses 'hacer': hace sol / calor / frío / viento. 'Está haciendo mucho sol' = it's really sunny right now.

examples.en: It's really sunny, put on sunscreen.

notes: Never 'está caliente' for weather. 'Tengo calor' = I'm hot (a person). 'Hace un calor horrible' = it's horribly hot.

examples.tl: Hace mucho calor, vamos por un agua.
examples.en: It's really hot, let's go get a water.

notes: 'Tengo frío' = I'm cold (a person). 'Hace un frío...' = it's freezing. 'Chamarra' (Mex) / 'chaqueta' = jacket.

examples.tl: En la noche hace frío, lleva chamarra.
examples.en: It gets cold at night, bring a jacket.

notes: 'Hace viento' / 'está ventoso'. In Mexico also 'aire': 'hay mucho aire'.

examples.en: The wind knocked the sign down.

notes: Mexicans often say 'hay mucho aire'; 'está ventoso' is also common.

examples.tl: Hace mucho viento en la playa hoy.
examples.en: It's really windy at the beach today.

notes: 'Tormenta eléctrica' = thunderstorm. 'Tormenta tropical' is one step below a 'huracán'. 'Trueno' = thunder, 'rayo' = lightning.

examples.tl: Hay alerta de tormenta para esta noche.
examples.en: There's a storm alert for tonight.

notes: Hurricane season in the Caribbean and Mexico: June–November. Plural: huracanes. 'Tocar tierra' = to make landfall.

examples.tl: El huracán tocó tierra en Cancún.
examples.en: The hurricane made landfall in Cancún.

notes: 'Está nublado' = it's cloudy. 'Nube' = cloud. 'Se nubló' = it clouded over.

examples.tl: Está nublado, seguro llueve en la tarde.
examples.en: It's cloudy, it'll surely rain this afternoon.

notes: '¡Qué + noun!' pattern: ¡Qué frío! ¡Qué lluvia! ¡Qué calorón! A very common complaint-greeting.

examples.tl: ¡Qué calor hace hoy, no se aguanta!
examples.en: It's so hot today, it's unbearable!

notes: 'Humedad' = humidity. Coastal cities are 'húmedas'; Mexico City is 'seca'. Also 'damp': ropa húmeda.

examples.tl: Veracruz es muy húmedo en verano.
examples.en: Veracruz is very humid in summer.

notes: 'Temporada seca' = dry season. 'Ley seca' = alcohol ban on election days. 'Secar' = to dry.

examples.tl: El clima aquí es seco y caluroso.
examples.en: The weather here is dry and hot.

notes: Rare in most of LatAm. 'Nevar' = to snow: 'está nevando'. In Mexico 'nieve' also = a sorbet / water-based ice cream.

examples.en: I've never seen snow.

notes: Celsius everywhere in LatAm: 30 grados = 86°F. 'Estamos a treinta grados' = it's 30 out. 'Bajo cero' = below zero.

examples.tl: Hoy estamos a treinta y dos grados.
examples.en: Today it's thirty-two degrees out.

notes: Colors agree in gender and number: rojo/roja/rojos/rojas. 'Colorado' = red in some regions.

examples.tl: El carro rojo es el mío.
examples.en: The red car is mine.

notes: 'En blanco' = blank. 'Arroz blanco' = white rice.

examples.en: I want a white shirt.

notes: Careful: 'negro/negra' is also used for people and can be a term of endearment ('mi negra') in Colombia and the Caribbean.

examples.en: I like black coffee.

notes: Same form masc./fem.: la casa azul. Plural: azules. 'Azul marino' = navy blue.

examples.tl: El cielo está muy azul hoy.
examples.en: The sky is really blue today.

notes: Same form masc./fem. Also 'unripe' (plátano verde) and 'dirty' (chiste verde = dirty joke). 'Salsa verde'.

examples.en: The avocado is still unripe.

notes: Double l: amarillo. Fem: amarilla.

examples.tl: Los taxis de Bogotá son amarillos.
examples.en: Bogotá's taxis are yellow.

notes: Both 'naranja' (invariable) and 'anaranjado' are used. 'La naranja' is also the fruit.

examples.en: My backpack is orange.

notes: 'Morado' is the everyday word in Mexico/Colombia; 'violeta' and 'lila' are also common. 'Un moretón' (or 'un morado') = a bruise.

examples.tl: La camioneta morada es de mi tía.
examples.en: The purple pickup is my aunt's.

notes: 'Rosa' (invariable) in Mexico; 'rosado' in Colombia, the Caribbean and South America. 'Una rosa' = a rose. 'Rosa mexicano' = hot pink.

examples.en: She ordered a pink dress.

notes: 'Café' = brown in Mexico, Central America and Colombia; 'marrón' in Argentina, the Caribbean and Spain. Also = coffee. Hair/eyes: 'castaño'.

examples.en: I have brown eyes.

notes: Same form masc./fem. Plural: grises. 'Un día gris' = a gray, gloomy day.

examples.en: It's a really gray day.

notes: Always 'de qué color', never 'qué color'. Answer: 'Es rojo.'

examples.en: What color is your car?

notes: Goes after the color: azul claro = light blue, verde claro. Also '¡Claro!' = of course, and 'clear'.

examples.tl: Quiero el azul claro, no el oscuro.
examples.en: I want the light blue one, not the dark one.

notes: 'Verde oscuro' = dark green. 'Está oscuro' = it's dark (out). 'Oscurecer' = to get dark.

examples.en: I prefer dark colors.

notes: Agrees when it precedes a noun: mucha gente, muchos tacos. As an adverb it's invariable: 'me gusta mucho'. 'Mucho gusto' = nice to meet you.

examples.tl: Hay mucha gente en el metro.
examples.en: There are a lot of people on the subway.

notes: 'Un poco' = a bit; 'poco' alone = not much. Agrees before nouns: poca agua, pocos días.

examples.en: I still speak little Spanish.

notes: 'Demasiado caro' = too expensive. Agrees before nouns: demasiadas personas. Colloquially also just 'a lot'.

examples.en: It's too expensive, thanks.

notes: From 'faltar' (works like gustar). 'Falta uno' = one is missing. '¿Cuánto falta?' = how much longer? 'Me falta dinero' = I'm short on money.

examples.en: How much longer until we get there?
There's a chair missing.

notes: 'Es suficiente' / 'ya es suficiente'. '¡Ya basta!' = enough, stop it. 'Alcanza' = it's enough (money, food).

examples.en: Is a hundred pesos enough?

notes: 'Lleno, por favor' at the gas station = fill it up. 'Estoy lleno' = I'm full (food). 'Está lleno' = it's packed.

examples.en: The parking lot is full.

notes: Accent on the í. 'El tanque está vacío'. The noun 'el vacío' = emptiness / the void.

examples.en: The bottle is empty.

notes: LatAm is metric: 1 kilo ≈ 2.2 lb. Market talk: '¿A cuánto el kilo?' 'Medio kilo', 'un cuarto'.

examples.tl: ¿A cuánto está el kilo de tomate?
examples.en: How much is a kilo of tomatoes?

notes: Deli counters sell by grams: 'doscientos gramos de jamón' = 200 g (a bit under half a pound).

examples.en: Give me three hundred grams of cheese.

notes: Gas, milk and water are sold by the liter (≈ 1 quart). 'Medio litro', 'litro y medio'.

examples.tl: Un litro de leche, por favor.
examples.en: A liter of milk, please.

notes: ≈ 3.3 ft. Also 'el metro' = the subway (Mexico City, Medellín, Santiago). 'Metros cuadrados' = square meters (apartments).

examples.tl: La tienda está a cien metros.
examples.en: The store is a hundred meters away.

notes: ≈ 0.62 miles. Distances and speed limits are in km. Accent on the ó.

examples.tl: El aeropuerto está a veinte kilómetros.
examples.en: The airport is twenty kilometers away.

notes: Market/bakery unit: 'una pieza de pan', '¿a cuánto la pieza?' = how much each? Also 'pieza' = part or (regional) room.

examples.tl: Los mangos están a diez pesos la pieza.
examples.en: The mangoes are ten pesos each.

notes: Buying pattern: 'dos kilos de...', 'medio kilo de...', 'un cuarto de...'. 'Me da' (usted) is the polite way to order.

examples.tl: Me da dos kilos de naranja, por favor.
examples.en: Give me two kilos of oranges, please.

notes: 'Paquete de galletas' = pack of cookies; also a delivery parcel. 'Paquetería' = courier service. Phone/internet plans are also 'paquetes'.

examples.tl: Ya llegó mi paquete de Amazon.
examples.en: My Amazon package arrived.

notes: 'Agua de botella' / 'agua embotellada' = bottled water. 'Garrafón' = the big 20 L water jug.

examples.tl: Una botella de agua, por favor.
examples.en: A bottle of water, please.

notes: 'Una lata de refresco / cerveza'. 'Dar lata' (Mex) = to be a pain, to bother. 'Enlatado' = canned.

examples.en: Can you get me a can of Coke?

notes: Grocery bag, and in Mexico also a handbag. '¿Quiere bolsa?' at checkout; bags often cost extra. 'Bolsa de trabajo' = job board.

examples.en: —Do you want a bag? —No thanks, I brought mine.

notes: Also 'la caja' = the checkout / cashier: 'pague en caja'. 'Cajero' = cashier or ATM (cajero automático).

examples.tl: Pase a la caja, por favor.
examples.en: Go to the register, please.

notes: '¿Cuánto es?' = how much (total)? '¿Cuánto cuesta?' = how much does it cost? '¿Cuánto tiempo?' = how long? Plural '¿cuántos?' = how many.

examples.en: How much is everything?

notes: Invariable: cada día, cada semana. 'Cada uno' = each one. '¿Cada cuánto?' = how often? 'Cada quince días' = every two weeks.

examples.en: How often does the bus come by?

notes: Prices and rates: 'cien pesos por hora', 'dos por uno' (2-for-1). 'Por ciento' = percent. 'Por día' = per day.

examples.en: They charge fifty pesos per hour.

notes: The noun: 'la mitad del precio' = half the price. 'A la mitad' = halfway / in the middle. The adjective is 'medio'.

examples.tl: Ya gasté la mitad del dinero.
examples.en: I've already spent half the money.

notes: 'El doble' = twice as much. 'Cuarto doble' = double room. 'Doble sentido' = double meaning (Mexican humor staple).

examples.en: They charged me double.

notes: Never 'muy mucho'; say 'muchísimo'. 'Muy bien' = very good / very well. Invariable.

examples.en: It's very far.

notes: 'Bastante bien' = pretty good. Before nouns = plenty of: 'bastante gente'. Also 'enough': 'ya es bastante'.

examples.en: The apartment is pretty big.

notes: 'Ya casi' = almost there / almost done. 'Casi casi' = very nearly. 'Casi nunca' = hardly ever.

examples.en: I'm almost there.

notes: Also 'just (now)' in LatAm: 'apenas llegué' = I just got here. 'Apenas ayer' = just yesterday.

examples.tl: Apenas me alcanza para la renta.
examples.en: I barely have enough for rent.
I just got here, give me a minute.

notes: 'Un poquito' is everywhere and friendlier. 'Un poco de' + noun: un poco de agua. 'Poquito a poquito' = little by little.

examples.en: I speak a little Spanish.

notes: Accent distinguishes it from 'mas' (but, literary). 'Más o menos' = so-so / more or less. 'Nada más' (Mex) = only, just. 'Más tarde' = later.

examples.en: Do you want more coffee?

notes: 'Al menos' / 'por lo menos' = at least. 'Menos mal' = thank goodness. Also clock time: 'las ocho menos diez'.

examples.en: There's less traffic today.

notes: Before adjectives/adverbs: 'tan caro', 'tan rápido'. 'Tan... como' = as... as. Use 'tanto' before nouns and after verbs.

examples.en: Don't be so dramatic!

notes: Agrees before nouns: tanta gente, tantos carros. After a verb it's invariable: 'no comas tanto'. 'No tanto' = not that much. '¡Tanto tiempo!' = long time!

examples.tl: Hay tanto tráfico que mejor camino.
examples.en: There's so much traffic that I'd rather walk.

notes: Colloquial intensifier all over LatAm: 'súper bien', 'súper caro', 'súper lejos'. Also 'el súper' = the supermarket.

examples.en: The food was really good.

notes: Mexican/Central American colloquial 'bien' + adj = very: 'está bien caro', 'bien bonito', 'bien lejos'. Standard 'bien' = well / fine / OK.

examples.en: That taco is really good.
Your house is really far.

notes: Rioplatense (Argentina/Uruguay) and Paraguay: 'rebueno', 'recaro', 're lindo'. Written attached or apart. Understood but not used in Mexico.

examples.en: That pizza is really good.
